Background Information on WinMaC competitionWinchester Math Competition (WinMaC) in MA is a non-profit math competition for any students grade 4-5.



This is a competition founded in 2016 by a group of middle school and high school students.



The problems will range in difficulty from advanced elementary to middle school math levels in the areas of number theory, algebra, geometry, counting and probability.



For more info, please visit: winchestermc.com

topics.title: Volume 1 Question
topics.text:
Hello! I was solving Volume 1 problems, I'm understanding most of the concepts in the entire book but I'm still stuck with a problem Chapter 4.



Here is the problem: Given that x is directly proportional to y and to z and is inversely proportional to w, and that x = 4 when (w, y, z) = (6, 8, 5), what is x when (w, y, z) = (4, 10, 9)?



Here is the solution: Because x is inversely proportional to w, when all other variables are constant, xw is constant. Similarly, when the other two variables are constant, each of x/y, and x/z is constant. We can combine all these by saying xw/yz is constant. Thus, from the problem we have (xw/yz = 4*6/8*5 = 3/5).



When (w,y,z) = (4, 10, 9) we find x = 3yz/5w = 27/2.



(Sorry AoPS if this violates any copyright laws)



This is all very abstract, and I'm not sure how we deduce that x is inversely proportional to w, and so on, and how we can combine all those constant elements to get xw/yz. Also, since x is directly proportional to y, if x = 4 when y = 8, doesn't that mean that x = 5 when y = 10...? Or am I just being stupid?



Thank you! :)

topics.title: Nice Rate Question
topics.text:
CMMS PG. 60 Problem 1.781:

Tejas begins to paint a fence that is 100 meters long at noon. By 2pm, Tejas has 1/3 of the fence painted and Jason arrives to help. At 3pm, 4/5 of the fence is painted and Tejas leaves Jason to finish painting the remaining fence. What times does Jason finish painting the fence?

My SolutionSo tejas paints $\frac{100}{3}$ meters of the fence in 2 hours. so he paints at a rate of $\frac{100}{6}$ fence per hour. Him and Jason are able to paint $\frac{400}{5} - \frac{100}{3} = \frac{700}{15}$ They do this in an hour so $\frac{700}{15} = (\frac{250}{15} + \frac{15r}{15})$ R is Jason's rate and I converted them to common fractions. So r=30. Since they painted 4/5 1/5 is remaining, which is 100/5=20 so 20=rt. The time is 2/3 hour or 40 minutes. he finished painting at 3:40

101 posts, not that impressive, but  I decided to post my story of how I got into mathcounts and started wanting to improve:



It all started last year in 7th grade. My math teacher saw that I was passionate about math and good at it in the classroom so, she recommended me to the MATHCOUNTS club teacher. I joined thinking that this would be a club where I would be able to do more math and just injoy the experience overall. Little did i now that the math would be much harder that i expected.

Qualifying's came along and i was feeling confident. Sadly for me, we did state qualifying's and i got destroyed. Honestly I don't know how. I didn't even make top 10 team. My friend, also in mathcounts, was the 10 person on the team. I was surprised since i did better in the classroom. So I made it a goal to beat him next year. My other friend who made top 4 chapter, started helping me. He said that i cound make state with help. (Our state cutoff 23 lol) I pushed it and said i want to make top 4. Again, little did i know that the cutoff for us was 32+. So i kind of gave up on that. Now I'm reading CMMS and i have vol 1 lined up. I aslo have a mathcounts tutor who i vist 1 a week during the school year. So far it has not been easy. My current goal right now is to score a 20+ on chapter sprint. Some of you can do that without scratch paper, I'm not you. CMMS has probably brought me the most trouble. I'm spending most of my summer in my room reading it.
